comparison: Canonical 1914 keys searched; all information-domain keys and adjacent principles inspected. Distinguish concrete transformation differences from upper-principle membership. No central files modified.

records.locator: Section 2, equation 3 and preceding telescoping expectation; pages 608-609
records.observation: Each level estimates its own adjacent difference; its two resolutions share one Brownian path. Levels are independently estimated. Finite maximum resolution retains discretization bias. The author's recursive-control-variate description is acknowledged; a known coarse expectation is not required.

records.locator: Section 2, page 3 randomized sum and equation 4 work bound
records.observation: Independent unbounded N includes difference i with positive probability P(N>=i); inverse inclusion weighting preserves the infinite telescoping expectation. Variance and expected work impose separate tail conditions. This is not a second application card for ordinary input importance sampling.

records.locator: Implementation steps 2-5, equation 5, page 490; accompanying MATLAB formula
records.observation: The author specifies independent symmetric Bernoulli perturbations and ghat=(yplus-yminus)/(2*c*delta) componentwise. Normal or uniform perturbations fail the cited inverse-moment conditions. One-measurement and second-order variants are not separately counted.

Gamma0(psi)(t)=psi(t)+sup[-psi(s)]positive over s<=t. The regulator increases only where the constrained path is zero. The card restricts to continuous paths and the one-sided map; the paper's two-sided extension is not another effect.

Strong Markov symmetry after first hitting gives P(S_t>=a,B_t<=b)=P(B_t>=2a-b), then the maximum tail equals twice the Gaussian endpoint tail. This rearranges path events rather than regulating paths or counting differentiable crossings.

records.locator: Section 5.2, Theorem 29 and following explanation, pages 46-47
records.observation: For continuous local martingale M starting at zero with infinite bracket, tau_s=inf{t:[M]_t>s} and B_s=M_tau_s is Brownian in F_tau_s. The theorem changes the clock, preserving the probability measure; this is distinct from state transformations and drift measure changes.

records.locator: Section 2.2.2, equation P(E)=g(P(E)), Remark 2.4 and extinction results
records.observation: Independent descendant trees produce the offspring-PGF fixed point, with extinction given by the smallest root on [0,1]. Iteration from zero is the finite-generation extinction recursion derived directly from the same independence. The always-one-child critical exception is explicitly retained.

Dyson identity splits the Liouville evolution into projected instantaneous drift, orthogonal dynamics and a history integral. Exact representation does not make the memory kernel cheap; finite-memory or Markovian approximations add assumptions. Quantum and fluid applications are not separate cards.

records.locator: Section 4 IST steps; Section 6.1 equations 6.1-6.3; introduction
records.observation: For KdV, eigenvalues are fixed while reflection data and norming constants acquire explicit time exponentials. Direct scattering followed by transformed-data inversion recovers the field. Marchenko kernels encode both discrete spectrum and reflection data. The paper's numerical coefficient realization is not counted separately.

records.locator: Section 1 equation 1.2 and Theorem 1; Section 2 accessory parameters
records.observation: Complex integration of corner-power factors fixes turning angles. Prevertices must also solve the side-length parameter problem; arbitrary prevertices need not give the desired sides or injectivity. Normalization removes conformal-map freedom. Disk versus half-plane formulations are one operation.

records.locator: Section 4 equation 4 orientation; Section 6 Pfaffian formula and planar specialization on page 205
records.observation: For genus zero the Kasteleyn formula reduces to one signed Pfaffian, whose magnitude is the weighted perfect-matching sum. The clockwise-odd face condition supplies the orientation signs. General surface multi-Pfaffian extensions are excluded; matching existence is not assumed for the count itself.

Regular-singularity coefficients define Q(alpha)=alpha(alpha-1)+f0*alpha+g0. Its roots set the power prefactors; equation 2.7.5 supplies the coefficient recurrence. Integer-separated roots require the possible logarithmic second solution in 2.7.6.

Canonical coordinates satisfy v(t)=0 and v(s)=1. The transformed equation is independent of s; introducing w=s_t lowers its order. Characteristics only compute the coordinates. Multiple reductions need the specified solvable-group structure.

records.locator: Section 4.2 equations 4.8-4.12; preceding analytic-strip error discussion
records.observation: x=tanh((pi/2)*sinh(t)) and its Jacobian yield double-exponential tails and the truncated trapezoidal rule. Nearby transformed complex singularities constrain the error. Single-exponential, half-line and oscillatory variants are not additional cards.

The dimension matrix has rank k; n-k independent null vectors form exponent columns for dimensionless monomials. Dimensional homogeneity reduces variables but does not supply a missing physical relation or constants. Individual Reynolds/Froude examples are excluded.
